name: Bronze Arrow Lettuce
summary: Bronze Arrow is a named looseleaf Lactuca sativa variety with bronze-tinted, arrow-shaped foliage. Cornell's 2019 summer trial provides one location-season snapshot; its results are not a universal performance guarantee.

identity.short: Named looseleaf variety with bronze-tinted foliage
identity.guidance: Cornell's citizen-science variety record classifies Bronze Arrow as looseleaf and describes dark red-green, arrow-shaped leaves with bronze tinting. This supports variety context, not a formal registration claim.

growth.short: Looseleaf form; no head-size target is established
growth.guidance: Cornell describes a looseleaf plant rather than a romaine or heading type. Its listed 46–60 day maturity is variety-directory information, not a controlled estimate for every site or indoor system; no mature dimensions are established here.

cultivation.short: One Cornell summer-trial result; keep its limits visible
cultivation.guidance: In Cornell's reported 2019 summer lettuce trial, Bronze Arrow's row recorded 7 oz, a disease score of 5/5, taste 4/5, bitterness 2/3, and zero plants bolted. The report says planting was May 29, harvest July 23, at one-foot spacing. This is one trial result, not proof of lasting disease resistance or universal slow-bolting performance.

care.short: Keep the shallow root zone evenly moist
care.guidance: UMN Extension explains that lettuce has shallow roots and can develop tipburn after a dry spell is followed by renewed water and growth. Check moisture consistency; do not infer that browned edges alone indicate disease or a nutrient deficiency. This is lettuce-level outdoor guidance, not an indoor watering schedule.

harvest.short: Pick leaves while tender; avoid delaying into bolting
harvest.guidance: As a looseleaf lettuce, Bronze Arrow can be harvested as usable leaves; UMN also describes repeated leaf picking when most small leaves remain, or cutting the whole plant. The Cornell trial recorded no bolting in its single summer trial, but that result is not a guaranteed harvest window for this variety.

problems.short: Heat and long days can still trigger bolting
problems.guidance: UMN Extension notes that heat and long days can cause lettuce to send up a flowering stalk; leaves may become bitter and the harvest ends. A zero-bolting result in Cornell's 2019 trial does not establish immunity or performance in other seasons. No specific Bronze Arrow disease resistance is asserted.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: The selected evidence does not establish hydroponic performance for Bronze Arrow.

growthHabits.reason: No consistently sourced controlled-vocabulary habit was selected.

spacing.reason: Field spacing is not a hydroponic position count.

light.reason: Outdoor lettuce guidance is not converted to indoor lamp intensity.

name: Breen Romaine Lettuce
summary: Breen is Johnny's named compact red mini-romaine variety. The seller reports an early compact mini head, 45 days to maturity, and an average height near 8 inches; these remain product-scoped claims.

metrics.label: Product-listed maturity
metrics.note: Johnny's estimate from seeding; not a guaranteed indoor harvest date.

identity.guidance: Johnny's identifies Breen as Lactuca sativa, open-pollinated, compact red mini-romaine. It is distinct from generic Romaine and Red Romaine identities.

growth.short: A short, compact mini head with bronze-red color
growth.guidance: Johnny's describes Breen as a very compact mini-romaine head that forms early and stays at mini size for a period; the seller reports an average height near 8 inches and bronze-red color. These are product-level characteristics, not a general dimension for romaine lettuce.

cultivation.short: Supplier reports greenhouse and hydroponic performance
cultivation.guidance: Johnny's lists Breen as a greenhouse and hydroponic performer. This supports the named product in the supplier's stated context, not a guarantee for every Garden system; field row spacing is not converted to pod spacing.

care.guidance: Lettuce has shallow roots; UMN Extension links moisture swings—especially renewed growth after dry soil—with tipburn. Keep the root zone consistently supplied in soil cultivation. No hydroponic irrigation interval is inferred.

harvest.short: Harvest as a mini head or pick leaves for a repeat cut
harvest.guidance: Johnny's describes Breen for mini heads and also as usable for cut-and-come-again harvest. Its 45-day maturity figure is a product estimate, not a guaranteed Garden harvest date. General lettuce guidance supports removing leaves while leaving most small leaves growing, or cutting the whole plant.

problems.short: Supplier lists downy-mildew resistance; bolting remains possible
problems.guidance: Johnny's lists high resistance for specified downy-mildew races (EU 16–21, 23–26, 28–37; US 5–9). This is the supplier's cultivar-specific rating, not immunity or a diagnosis. Like lettuce generally, Breen can still bolt under heat and long-day conditions; the species-level warning is not a Breen-specific heat threshold.

evidence.note: Johnny's labels Breen a hydroponic performer; this is not a system-specific yield guarantee.
Supplier describes an early compact mini head.

height.reason: The source gives average height for the mini stage, not a mature height range.

spacing.reason: No pod spacing or universal Garden position count established.

light.reason: Outdoor crop guidance is not mapped to indoor grow-light intensity.

name: Muir Lettuce
summary: Muir is a named Batavian lettuce variety. Johnny's reports heat tolerance, slower bolting in its summer trials, a compact dense head that can be harvested mini or full-size, and hydroponic performance; these are seller-scoped claims.

metrics.label: Product-listed maturity
metrics.note: Johnny's estimate; conditions and transplant timing affect maturity.

identity.guidance: Johnny's lists Muir as Lactuca sativa and technically a Batavian type. This named variety remains distinct from general lettuce or romaine types.

growth.short: Wavy leaves form dense heads from mini to full size
growth.guidance: Johnny's describes light-green, extra-wavy leaves forming dense heads that can be picked at mini size or allowed to bulk into large full-size heads. These are Muir product characteristics; no numeric mature dimensions are provided here.

cultivation.short: Seller reports heat tolerance and hydroponic performance
cultivation.guidance: Johnny's describes Muir as heat tolerant and slow to bolt in its summer trials, and lists hydroponic suitability. These supplier-reported cultivar claims do not establish a precise indoor climate setpoint, nutrient target, or system layout.

care.short: Steady moisture supports even lettuce growth
care.guidance: UMN Extension notes that lettuce has shallow roots and that a dry spell followed by renewed watering and growth can lead to tipburn. Use this as general lettuce care guidance; it is not a diagnosis of Muir or a nutrient recipe.

harvest.guidance: Johnny's describes Muir heads as harvestable at mini size or after further bulking, and lists an average 50 days to maturity from seeding. The timing is a supplier estimate and not a guaranteed indoor harvest date.

problems.short: Resistance ratings are specific to the seller-listed races and pests
problems.guidance: Johnny's lists high resistance to downy mildew EU races 16–26, 28, 32 and US races 5–9, lettuce leaf aphid, and Tomato Bushy Stunt Virus; it lists intermediate resistance to Lettuce Mosaic Virus. These are seller ratings, not immunity and not a substitute for diagnosis. General lettuce can still bolt under stress; Muir's slower bolting claim is limited to the supplier's summer trials.

evidence.note: Johnny's labels Muir a hydroponic performer; no system-specific yield is inferred.
Supplier describes dense heads at small size; compact is used only for the reported mini stage.

spacing.reason: No pod spacing or universal Garden position count established.

light.reason: Outdoor crop guidance is not mapped to indoor grow-light intensity.

name: Pandero Romaine Lettuce
summary: Pandero is a supplier-listed red romaine with dense heads. Adaptive Seeds describes slow bolting, heat and cold tolerance, downy-mildew resistance, and about 30 days for baby leaves or 60 for a full head; these remain supplier-scoped claims.

metrics.label: Supplier maturity estimate
metrics.value: 30 days baby leaf; 60 days full head
metrics.note: Adaptive Seeds product estimate; not a guaranteed indoor or local harvest date.

identity.guidance: Adaptive Seeds lists Pandero as Lactuca sativa and red romaine. The supplier listing supports this named product identity but does not establish independent cultivar registration.

growth.short: Dense red heads; color develops early per supplier
growth.guidance: Adaptive Seeds describes Pandero as a deep-red version of Winter Density, with dense heads and early-developing red color. This is a supplier description, not a claim that it is genetically identical to Winter Density.

cultivation.short: Supplier describes cool- and warm-weather tolerance
cultivation.guidance: Adaptive Seeds describes Pandero as slow to bolt and tolerant of heat and cold. Keep these as product claims: no numeric temperature limits, indoor spacing, or hydroponic performance is established. General lettuce guidance still favors steady moisture and cool-season growth.

care.short: Avoid moisture swings in the shallow root zone
care.guidance: UMN Extension describes lettuce as shallow-rooted and associates tipburn with a dry spell followed by renewed water and growth. Maintain more even soil moisture; this crop-level advice does not establish an indoor watering interval for Pandero.

harvest.short: Supplier lists baby-leaf and full-head windows
harvest.guidance: Adaptive Seeds lists about 30 days for baby leaves and 60 days for full heads. These are product estimates; they vary with conditions and are not guaranteed Garden dates. USU describes cos/romaine harvest at early heading, while general lettuce can also be picked as leaves.

problems.short: Downy-mildew resistance is a supplier claim, not immunity
problems.guidance: Adaptive Seeds lists Pandero as resistant to downy mildew and describes slow bolting, but does not provide race coverage or a rating scale on the selected product listing. Treat this as supplier-scoped information, not guaranteed protection; no other disease resistance is inferred.

growthHabits.reason: The red-romaine type is described, but no controlled-vocabulary habit is established for the named product.

spacing.reason: Field spacing is not converted to system position count.

light.reason: Outdoor crop guidance is not mapped to indoor lamp intensity.

name: Lady Murasaki Komatsuna
variety: Lady Murasaki named komatsuna selection; formal cultivar status not asserted
summary: Lady Murasaki is a named komatsuna selection within Brassica rapa. Fedco describes upright, deep-purple leaves and estimates 45 days to maturity; these traits and timing remain product-scoped.

identity.short: Named komatsuna selection within Brassica rapa
identity.guidance: Fedco lists Lady Murasaki as a named komatsuna selection, and Kew accepts Brassica rapa. The product name is retained without asserting formal cultivar registration; seed-lot genetics are documented separately in the Seed Profile.

growth.short: Supplier describes rounded, deep-purple leaves about 8–10 inches long
growth.guidance: Fedco describes slow-growing, rounded deep-purple leaves that stand upright and gives an approximate leaf length of 8–10 inches. These are seller-described product traits, not a measured whole-plant height or spread; no mature dimensions are inferred.

cultivation.short: Cool-season Asian-green crop; no indoor settings established
cultivation.guidance: Johnny's general Asian-greens guide gives a broad sowing season from early spring through midsummer and late-fall sowing only in mild or protected conditions. This is production guidance for the group, not a Lady Murasaki indoor temperature, nutrient recipe or system spacing. Oregon State describes komatsuna as a bunching green with dark leaves and slender petioles, at crop-type scope.

care.short: Monitor flea-beetle feeding in outdoor beds
care.guidance: Johnny's Asian-greens guide identifies flea beetles as a production pest and recommends floating row cover from sowing in field settings. Apply that as outdoor exclusion guidance only; it is not a treatment for indoor plants and does not establish Lady Murasaki resistance.

harvest.short: Supplier lists about 45 days; harvest stage depends on intended size
harvest.guidance: Fedco lists 45 days to maturity and describes mild leaves; treat the timing as a supplier estimate, not a fixed home-system date. Johnny's says komatsuna heading types may be harvested at medium or full size and are suited to a single harvest. UCANR's regional mustard guidance also describes harvesting young leaves at about 4–5 in (10–13 cm), taking the whole plant, or picking outer leaves so inner leaves continue developing. Those are crop/regional options, not a Lady Murasaki-specific repeat-harvest guarantee.

problems.short: Warm weather can trigger bolting; scout leaves for flea-beetle shot holes
problems.guidance: UCANR notes that mustard greens may bolt when weather warms and days lengthen; this is a crop-level seasonal signal, not a Lady Murasaki-specific threshold. University of Minnesota Extension describes flea-beetle feeding as many small, round holes in leaves and recommends row covers as an exclusion method for cole crops. Johnny's also recommends floating row cover for Asian greens. These sources do not establish cultivar resistance, and row covers are outdoor management rather than an indoor treatment.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: No evidence establishes this selection's hydroponic performance.

growthHabits.reason: No normalized habit established from the selected evidence.

spacing.reason: Garden-system position count is not established.

light.reason: Outdoor crop guidance is not mapped to indoor lamp intensity.

name: Scarlet Red Tatsoi
variety: Scarlet Red Tatsoi; supplier-listed red selection, formal cultivar status not asserted
summary: Scarlet Red Tatsoi is a supplier-listed red selection of Brassica rapa tatsoi. Hudson Valley Seed describes plum-colored leaves, a semi-heading rosette and container use; its flea-beetle tolerance statement is explicitly tentative.

identity.short: Supplier-listed red tatsoi selection within Brassica rapa
identity.guidance: Hudson Valley Seed lists Scarlet Red Tatsoi as Brassica rapa; Kew accepts B. rapa. North Carolina State Extension describes tatsoi as B. rapa var. rosularis. The product name is retained without claiming formal cultivar registration or a separate accepted species.

growth.short: Semi-heading rosette with plum leaves and bright-green stems
growth.guidance: Hudson Valley Seed describes Scarlet Red's plum-colored leaves, bright-green stems and semi-heading rosette; NC State's broader tatsoi entry describes a low, flat rosette with thick spoon-shaped leaves. The supplier's 12-inch height and 16-inch width are estimates for this product, not guarantees across systems or for all tatsoi.

cultivation.short: Supplier lists full sun and container suitability; pod spacing remains unknown
cultivation.guidance: Hudson Valley Seed lists full sun (8+ hours) and container suitability for Scarlet Red. NC State describes tatsoi as a cool-weather crop and notes full sun or partial shade at species/type scope. The product page's 6-inch field spacing is not converted into a Garden pod count; no nutrient recipe or household hydroponic compatibility is established.

care.short: Harvest the intended form; do not assume repeated regrowth
care.guidance: Hudson Valley Seed says Scarlet Red may be grown for baby clippings or to a full rosette, but its growing instructions specifically recommend whole-head harvest and say it is not ideal as cut-and-come-again. Follow that product-specific instruction rather than generalizing repeated cutting from other Asian greens.

harvest.short: Supplier estimates about 50 days to a whole head
harvest.guidance: Hudson Valley Seed lists 50 days to maturity and directs growers to harvest the whole head. This is a supplier estimate, not a guaranteed date; local conditions and the chosen baby-leaf versus full-rosette stage affect timing. Avoid promising multiple harvests from this selection.

problems.short: Heat, inadequate water and flea beetles can disrupt tatsoi
problems.guidance: NC State Extension reports that higher temperatures and inadequate water can cause tatsoi to bolt, reducing harvest quality, and lists slugs, snails, cutworms and flea beetles as potential problems. Hudson Valley Seed says Scarlet Red may be less affected by flea beetles because of its dark color, but labels this as possible; it is not an established resistance rating.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: Container suitability does not establish hydroponic performance.

growthHabits.reason: Rosette morphology is supported for tatsoi crop type, but Compatibility Profile V1 has no horticultural-type taxonomic scope; the claim remains only in the scoped Plant Profile section.

evidence.note: Supplier estimate of 12 in high converted to 30.48 cm; approximate outdoor product dimension, not a guarantee across systems.
Supplier estimate of 16 in wide converted to 40.64 cm; approximate outdoor product dimension, not a Garden system spacing rule.

spacing.reason: The supplier's 6-inch field spacing does not define a Garden pod count.

evidence.note: Supplier-listed outdoor exposure for this Scarlet Red product; not an indoor grow-light classification.

name: Green Salanova Lettuce
variety: Green Salanova range/type; exact commercial variety not specified
summary: Green Salanova represents a branded group of green Lactuca sativa types, not one exact cultivar. Rijk Zwaan describes its range as suitable for commercial hydroponic production and a one-cut harvest; University of Minnesota Extension supplies separate crop-level guidance on cool conditions, repeated leaf harvest and bolting.

identity.short: Green Salanova brand group; exact variety unresolved
identity.guidance: Rijk Zwaan describes Salanova as a brand range containing multiple lettuce types and varieties, available in green and red. Kew accepts Lactuca sativa. This identity represents the green Salanova group named in the reference context; it is not promoted to a single cultivar or specific leaf/head form.

growth.short: Many baby-sized leaves; Salanova types vary
growth.guidance: Rijk Zwaan describes the Salanova range as producing numerous baby-sized leaves in several lettuce types. Its ‘one cut, ready’ description refers to cutting the head at the base and separating the leaves; it is a brand-level harvest presentation, not a claim that every green selection has the same shape or mature dimensions.

cultivation.short: Commercial hydroponics documented; household system details remain open
cultivation.guidance: Rijk Zwaan says Salanova is well suited to hydroponic production as whole heads at high density. This supports the branded range at commercial-production scope; it does not establish performance in every home unit, pod count, nutrient recipe or exact unresolved green variety. For lettuce crop care, University of Minnesota Extension recommends cool-season conditions and keeping soil moist; its regional field spacing is not converted to Garden system spacing.

harvest.short: One-cut head harvest; crop-level leaf picking also documented
harvest.guidance: Rijk Zwaan describes Salanova’s ‘one cut, ready’ approach: cut the head at the base to release baby-sized leaves. Separately, University of Minnesota Extension says lettuce leaves can be picked once usable; leaving most small leaves can allow multiple harvests, while the whole plant can also be cut at or just above the soil. The repeat-cut guidance is general lettuce crop evidence, not a guarantee for an unspecified Salanova type.

problems.short: Heat and long days can trigger bolting
problems.guidance: University of Minnesota Extension reports that heat and long days can trigger lettuce bolting; leaves may become tough or bitter and harvest ends when the plant bolts. This is crop-level lettuce guidance, not a Salanova-specific heat-tolerance rating. No cultivar resistance is inferred.

needsValidation.short: Exact green Salanova variety and home-system performance remain unresolved
needsValidation.guidance: The commercial range contains multiple varieties and lettuce forms. A packet or breeder variety name is needed for cultivar-specific dimensions, maturity and resistance. Commercial hydroponic suitability does not establish fit, spacing or nutrient targets for a particular Garden system.

evidence.note: Rijk Zwaan describes Salanova as suited to commercial hydroponic whole-head production at high density. This is range-level evidence, not a home-system guarantee, pod-spacing rule or nutrient prescription.

growthHabits.reason: The range includes different lettuce types and forms.

height.reason: No exact variety or numeric dimensions selected.

spread.reason: No exact variety or numeric dimensions selected.

spacing.reason: Commercial high-density production does not establish pod count or spacing for a Garden system.

light.reason: General lettuce outdoor guidance is not mapped to indoor grow-light intensity.
